checks: No fully captured interval means every lower endpoint is negative for the closed cap. The cap mass is the sum of positive upper parts even when some intervals are missed or only touch zero.
The zero first moment gives Q/2=Σw_i r_i. Replacing negative upper endpoints by zero and bounding each width by H proves the first bound without a base arrangement or compatibility.

Cauchy on the other N−1 widths gives the claimed ratio algebra. Its simplification was checked symbolically. AM–GM gives the constant 2/(1+√N), and the single interval is centered with exactly half its mass captured.
Original b9d705e0e5ad374f §7 (7) explicitly states the independent finite-family bound.

overlap.comparison: It proves the same first estimate on actual compatible integer fibers with integer-base centroid and then the stricter one-third consequence of concave widths. This draft extends the first estimate to arbitrary separate intervals and adds a finite-N constant with no compatibility assumption.

readability: The proof is readable as stated.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The exact moment identity and Cauchy–AM–GM yield both bounds for arbitrary separate interval measures with no fully captured interval.
